verdict.rationale: Battery and power efficiency are a fair axis for any CPU, so the story applies, but the evidence shows no support for it on this chip. Intel itself positions the 285K as a desktop part. The battery-life and 'slim design' claims come from Core Ultra family marketing pages, not the 285K, and community reviews only note better efficiency and relaxed cooling versus the 14900K in desktop use. Nothing shows fanless or battery-powered designs or any battery-life testing.

support.subject: As a power-user, this chip powers thin, quiet, all-day-battery machines — shipping in fanless or low-power designs with credible battery-life evidence
